doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Better with age and closing
summary: Being a better musician at 75, thanks, and goodbyes.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: No, no, no. You said it in one of your thoughts, you said “I’m definitely a better musician at 71 than I was at 21.”
You are too. God I’ve known you since 1995. You’re way smarter. Man, you’re way smarter.
I’m going to have to get that in writing, Bill.
Well I want to thank you.
I didn’t mean to ramble so long. You knew it — when you called me you knew what you were in for just like Billy Mitchell. You knew you were going to catch hell.
I liked it. I appreciate your time.
Hey man, it’s been an honor.

Well thank you very much, and best of luck with that new recording, and I enjoy your outlook on life. I can relate very well to it, making a living in music by doing whatever comes up and doing it well.
I’ll see you on the flip side. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
